solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Saw book on establishment figure?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: one who establishes a fact, as a theorem is established, is a prover; the question mark flags the pun
B is the standard abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a book resting on a pillar of the Establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense but is the noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional maxim or adage, which is exactly what a proverb is.

clue.text: Each year an idol enters temple

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so it is placed within the other letters

blocks.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year
an idol is a false god
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Every year a statue of a deity is carried into a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Per annum, Latin for 'by the year', is the source of the abbreviation for 'each year'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower that serves as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in Asia.

clue.text: Drink too much perhaps where meeting takes place

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two parts: over plus lap, to lap being to drink, so a whimsical over-drinking
second meaning: the region where two things meet and share space

explanation.surface: Someone overindulges at the bar where the get-together is held.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps' flags the first sense as a playful split of the word, since cats lap milk.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlap is the area two things share where they meet, and split apart it suggests lapping beyond the limit.

clue.text: Spellbound's opening credits using only central character

indicators.note: keeping only the central character means just the middle letter survives

blocks.note: an opening such as a door is an entrance
the middle letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: The opening credits of the film Spellbound show only its star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spellbound's' looks like the Hitchcock film owning the credits; it is the definition with 's as is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone entranced is held as if by a spell, captivated or spellbound.

clue.text: Satellite company receiving wider coverage

indicators.note: the second piece is received inside the covering supplied by the first

blocks.note: wider means broader, here acting as the outer cover
a theatre company is its cast

explanation.surface: A satellite TV firm is getting more extensive news coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite company' reads as one phrase, but only 'Satellite' defines; 'company' is a theatre troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A communications satellite transmits signals to receivers below, acting as a broadcaster.

clue.text: Where one naturally is somewhat absorbed by what goes over one's head

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken right inside another thing, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: headwear sits on top of the head
somewhat means a bit, to some degree

explanation.surface: A riddle about something partly soaked up by whatever passes overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbed' suggests soaking up liquid, but here it only means one piece is held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home environment of an animal or plant, the place it naturally lives.

clue.text: Get in the way of sacking a poor performer

indicators.note: sacking someone removes them, so these letters are dropped

blocks.note: to hamper is to obstruct or get in the way of
a means per, as in two pounds a head

explanation.surface: Obstructing the dismissal of an incompetent actor.
explanation.walkthrough: HAMPER loses PER. 'Sacking' looks like hessian cloth, but it means firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a bad actor who overacts, a poor performer on stage.

clue.text: Meat packing company in embargo

indicators.note: packing something means wrapping it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: an embargo is an official ban on trade
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A meat-packing firm is caught in a trade embargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork, a kind of meat.

clue.text: Rent business causing disruption is source of cyclical upheaval

blocks.note: rent is the past participle of rend, to tear
ado is fuss or troublesome business

explanation.surface: A landlord's rent business is upsetting tenants with recurring turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is the past form of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a rotating windstorm whose spinning column wrecks what it passes over.

clue.text: Parody attempt to win cycling match

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, so the last letter comes to the front
an attempt to win surrounds and captures its prize, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: an attempt is a try
a vesta is a short match for striking

explanation.surface: A sports parody: someone's bid to win a bicycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a contest but is a light; a vesta is an old name for a short wax match.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque or absurd imitation, a mocking parody.

clue.text: Prepare to hold new suite short of one place for visitor

indicators.note: being short of one means lacking a single letter i, the roman numeral for one
making something new rearranges it into a fresh form
to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to groom is to prepare or train someone, or to smarten up
taken as written, before losing its I

explanation.surface: A hotelier gets a new suite ready, one room short, for an arriving guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the roman numeral I, and the shuffled remainder sits after the first letter of the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest room is a bedroom kept for people staying over, so it is a place for a visitor.

clue.text: Leader of Costa Rica changed around

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, at the front
letters that are changed are put into a different order

blocks.note: the opening letter of Costa
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The head of Costa Rica is a changed person, come round to a new view.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is the Latin-derived word used before dates or numbers to mean approximately.

clue.text: Code word is distributed when key part goes to terminal

indicators.note: going to the terminal means moving to the end of the line, so one letter is shifted to the last place

blocks.note: cards that are distributed are dealt
the key, or central, letter of the word, which is also a musical key

explanation.surface: A cipher is handed out once a vital section reaches the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: DEALT has its central letter A moved to the end. 'Key' does double duty: central, and A as a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the NATO phonetic alphabet's code word for the letter D.

clue.text: Describe energy policy inspired by court

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so it ends up inside another piece

blocks.note: to court someone is to go out with them, to date
E is the physics symbol for energy
a policy is a line, as in the party line

explanation.surface: An energy policy shaped by a judicial ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like the law court but is the verb, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to set out or portray something precisely, which is to describe it.

clue.text: Least constrained and abundant form of plant life

blocks.note: least constrained is loosest
rife means widespread or abundant

explanation.surface: Wild and abundant growth is a feature of unrestrained vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosestrife is a flowering plant, purple or yellow, growing by water.

clue.text: Popular entertainment magazine's left without article

indicators.note: being without something means it has been taken away

blocks.note: The Spectator is a British weekly political magazine, plus the possessive S
aport is a nautical word for to the left, the port side
the indefinite article, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A popular magazine has quit, leaving without the article it promised.
explanation.walkthrough: APORT drops its A (article) to leave PORT. 'Left' looks like a past tense, but it is the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator sport is a game that draws crowds of watchers, a form of mass entertainment.

clue.text: What's associated with wind and frost potentially?

definitions.text: What's associated with wind and frost potentially?

indicators.note: potentially means what these letters could become if rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weather riddle: what comes with wind and frost?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, since drifts are piled by wind in wintry weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowdrift is a bank of snow heaped up by the wind, typical of freezing weather.

clue.text: Forgetfulness of wife leaving violin bow out

indicators.note: a person leaving goes away, so that letter is dropped
out suggests disordered, put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife, the letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forgetful wife walks out leaving her violin bow behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of being forgotten or of forgetting everything.

clue.text: Accompanying article direct, but irrelevant

blocks.note: to be beside someone is to be alongside, accompanying them
the definite article
to point is to direct, as in pointing someone the way

explanation.surface: An accompanying piece of writing is forthright yet beside the matter at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beside the point does not bear on the matter being discussed, so it is irrelevant.

clue.text: Compiling crosswords is getting harder

blocks.note: first meaning: a crossword compiler is called a setter
second meaning: concrete or glue firming up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a setter's boast that puzzles are getting tougher; 'harder' means firmer, not more difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters set puzzles, and something that sets turns solid, so both senses share one word.

clue.text: Briefly screen observers in gallery after reporter's arrest

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the word, so we go by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: nick is British slang for arrest
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Watchers in an art gallery are screened after a journalist is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observers' are the eyes, and briefly screening them is a blink. 'After' puts TATE second.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictate is to blink or wink, momentarily covering the eyes with the lids.

clue.text: Customer's legal right framed by court

indicators.note: a picture framed by something is enclosed by it on all sides

blocks.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A customer's legal entitlement is set out by a court.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's makes 'Customer's' stand for 'customer is', the definition plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a customer of a professional service or business.

clue.text: Explain the significance of rabies initially spreading between domesticated animals?

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows
spreading here means working its way into, so one letter is placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: inter is the Latin prefix for between
a pet is a domesticated animal; the plural is a looseness
the first letter of rabies

explanation.surface: A vet considers what it means when rabies spreads among household pets.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'animals' though a single domestic animal is all the wordplay needs, a small looseness.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to explain the meaning or significance of something.

clue.text: Crest of bird having no role

indicators.note: having no part means that part is absent, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a partridge is a game bird
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: A bird's crest has no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crest' looks like a bird's tuft of feathers; it is the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow hilltop, the crest of a range.

clue.text: Transfer possibly secured as Oxford receives backing

indicators.note: something given backing is pushed from behind, so it is read back to front

blocks.note: an Oxford is a lace-up shoe, so it is secured by being laced

explanation.surface: A transfer student's place at Oxford University is secured once funding arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is the shoe, not the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A decal is a design printed on special paper for transferring onto another surface, so it is one kind of transfer.

clue.text: The author had written about story-teller briefly in action-packed epic

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: the setter is I, and I had written in contracted form is I'D
a liar tells stories in the sense of falsehoods

explanation.surface: A writer claims to have composed a gripping epic about a teller of tales.
explanation.walkthrough: LIAR is trimmed to LIA and wrapped by I'D. 'The author' is the crossword-setter speaking of themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad is the epic poem of the Trojan War, full of battle scenes.

clue.text: Remove qualification about wearing best clothes

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the next
to clothe something is to cover it, so it sits wrapped inside

blocks.note: the elite are the best of a group
an MA, Master of Arts, is a degree
someone wearing a coat is in it

explanation.surface: Take away a credential from someone dressed in their Sunday best.
explanation.walkthrough: A Russian-doll clue: three layers, each wrapping the next, with 'about' and 'clothes' as the two wrappers.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to get rid of something, taking it out entirely.

clue.text: Take in common feature of greatest weather threats

indicators.note: a feature common to several words is a run of letters that each one contains

blocks.note: the same three letters sit inside each of these three words

explanation.surface: The thing shared by the worst storms and gales.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, the letters appear in all three words at once rather than spanning a word break.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in food is to eat it, consuming it as a meal.

clue.text: Disregard information about half-cut academic

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards
half-cut means half of the word is chopped off

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
a lecturer is a university academic

explanation.surface: Ignore the reports about a tipsy professor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims LECTURER to its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to pay it no attention, to disregard it.

clue.text: In the absence of leader, staff handle request urgently

indicators.note: with no leader present, the word lacks its first letter

blocks.note: the staff of a firm are its men, its workforce
to handle someone a certain way is to treat them

explanation.surface: With the boss away, employees deal with an urgent request.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly, which is to ask urgently.
